verdict.rationale: pnpm's own CLI demonstrably rewrites the manifest and lockfile: a documented install mode "only updates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `package.json`", and `pnpm update` is named as a first-party upgrade command. However, the pack never documents `pnpm add` or `pnpm remove`, so only the upgrade leg and generic manifest/lockfile rewriting are evidenced. missing for 10: explicit documentation of add and remove commands, detail on how upgrades rewrite version ranges and the lockfile safely, independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-safe manifest editing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can add, remove, and upgrade dependencies through CLI commands that safely rewrite the manifest and lockfile, so an agent never hand-edits them

citations.quote: When used, only updates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `package.json`. Nothing gets written to the `node_modules` directory.
`pnpm update` will only add 1 new file to the store, instead of cloning the entire dependency just for the singular change.
